evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: I need your ten to fifteen minutes to discuss your move. Yes, sure. Perfect, thank you. [No explicit wait for confirmation of the 10-15 min + dependable quote framing; rep moves forward immediately.]
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: You're looking at doing it tomorrow, is that right? [Tomorrow confirmed.] Are you just moving within the same apartment complex? [Route confirmed.] Do you know the square footage of the two apartments? [~1000 noted.] What are the items left that we need to move for you? [Items listed.]
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Before I start, do you have any important concerns or instructions to take note of right now? [Asked at open.] Wanda responds: I was just trying to see how much will be because I started to move all my stuff but it's just me and a young daughter that I have, and it's been a little frustrating. I mean, I can't by myself.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep acknowledges: Of course, I know. I understand especially with the bigger items. That's okay, I'll explain all of that for you. [No follow-up dig; moves to logistics immediately rather than exploring the frustration or capacity constraint further.]
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: [None provided; rep acknowledges but does not reflect back the concerns in summary form.]
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment, different buildings), floors (second floor both), walking distance (door right beside stairs), truck parking (20-30 ft moving out, 20-50 ft moving in), items (couch, two beds, small fridge, freezer, washer, dryer), no boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: $97 per hour per mover, two men $194. Range given: $485 (2.5 hrs minimum), $582 (3 hrs), $776 (4 hrs). Personalized to stairs and bigger items only.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Includes two men, truck, everything they need, taxes, insurance, fuel, transportation. No hidden fees, no credit card fees, no assembly/reassembly fees. Two and a half hour minimum, 15-minute intervals after. [Full fee disclosure and commitment framing delivered.]
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: [Not asked. Rep moves from estimate directly into availability discussion: 'Let's see for now our availability is tomorrow and the next one would be on Wednesday already.']
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: On time guarantee if we run late, we provide discounts for your move. [Fully delivered with discount terms.]
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: We include our no worries, damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any accidental damages. [Coverage and amount stated, but no explicit mention of 'no deductible,' 'no fine print,' or that it's built into the rate, not an add-on.]
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: [No closing question asked; rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar.]
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: [Not asked. Rep ends with 'So I send everything in an email as well. So you can, just reply, reply to the email or give us a call. Whichever works for you.' No genuine 'What's still concerning you?' framing.]
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: [Never asked. Wanda defers: 'I will see how much of items I can move between today as of today and then I'll call again to make sure.' Rep accepts without an explicit 'Would you like our help with your move?' ask.]

top_strength: Joanna gathered all critical logistics details (floors, walking distances, truck parking, furniture list) efficiently and delivered a transparent, anchored estimate with strong pricing framing and fee disclosure.
coaching_note: Close the sale: after pricing, ask 'Does that feel fair?' and hold silence for the customer's response; then move to an explicit 'Would you like our help with your move?' and confirm booking details (date, time window, phone, addresses, crew size) before hanging up — currently the call ends without either a genuine price confirmation or any booking commitment.
